put capital in, on the pool's approved rail

A journey saved to this app, while it's built on the live contract
Record that a document was shown, or consent given or withdrawn

tools.name: accept_workspace_invite
tools.title: Join a workspace
tools.description: Accept an invitation to a workspace (list_my_invitations). You join with the role it names. A developer invitation also makes you a developer on Mynt if your account is just a user's; it never changes a firm's account (vendor, licence or liquidity provider), an admin's, or roles a Mynt admin set for you after it was sent.

tools.name: acknowledge_breach
tools.title: Acknowledge a covenant breach
tools.description: Licence provider: record that your firm has seen a breach (who and when). It stops nothing and clears nothing.

tools.name: add_agreement_audit_requirement
tools.title: Add an oversight audit to an agreement
tools.description: Licence provider (a member of the agreement's counterparty firm): add an oversight audit you run on the app under a program agreement with your firm, from the proposal on (so it can come with your terms): its name, kind, cadence (once, monthly, quarterly, annual, or on_change: each time the app's builds give it new verified source, or when you open one by hand), the first due date (not for on_change), what it covers and the evidence you need. Once the agreement is signed, Mynt opens each audit when it's time (monthly 14 days before it's due, quarterly 30, annual 60) and the next when one closes. Audited; the app's side sees it in list_agreement_audits.

first_due.description: YYYY-MM-DD; required unless cadence is on_change

evidence_required.description: What the app's side must submit

tools.name: add_entity_member
tools.title: Add someone to a firm
tools.description: Admin: make a signed-in user a member of a firm (they then act for it as a builder, a vendor or a licence provider, by their roles). The firm's existing members are told, on its webhooks (firm.member_added) and as a notice each. A licence-provider account added to a licence provider that already has one waits for an existing member to accept it (decide_firm_member).

tools.name: add_party
tools.title: Add a party to your firm's roster
tools.description: Add who fills a role at your firm: an internal person or an external legal entity, the mandatory stakeholders they fill on the licences you hold (fills: licence id + stakeholder id from the licence type's mandatory_stakeholders, see get_regulator), facts for the stakeholders' qualification criteria, and for counterparties the relationship. Products can only name parties on this roster. get_my_entity shows each licence's stakeholders reconciled against it.

kind.description: internal: a person in the firm (e.g. the compliance officer); external: another firm (e.g. the statutory auditor, a lending partner)

legal_entity_id.description: For external parties: a legal entity already on Mynt

new_legal_entity.description: For external parties not on Mynt yet: registers the legal entity first (its licences then need registering and verifying)

stakeholder.description: A mandatory stakeholder id on that licence type

attributes.description: Facts checked against the stakeholders' qualification criteria, e.g. { years_experience: 12, resident: true }

relationship.description: For counterparties, what ties you, e.g. collection_agency_agreement

tools.name: add_risk
tools.title: Add a risk to a register
tools.description: Add a risk to an app's or a financial product's risk register (the app's workspace owners and admins, or the product's own firm), or, for Mynt's admins, to the platform's own (subject_type platform, subject_id mynt). Give a title, a category (security, fraud, vendor, conduct, operational, compliance, credit, liquidity, other), how likely it is and how bad it would be (1-5 each; the score is their product: 1-4 low, 5-9 medium, 10-14 high, 15-25 critical), and optionally a description, the mitigation, its owner (a member of the app's workspace or the product's firm, a Mynt admin for the platform's; you by default) and the date it's next reviewed by. It starts open. Audited.

subject_id.description: The app's id, the product's id, or mynt for the platform's register

tools.name: admin_change_workspace_member_role
tools.title: Change a member's role in any workspace
tools.description: Admin: change a member's role in any workspace (owner, admin or member), as change_member_role does for its owners: the organization agrees first, a workspace always keeps an owner, and a demotion to member cuts their elevated access.

tools.name: admin_get_app
tools.title: One app, as an admin sees it
tools.description: Admin: one app with its workspace, owner, stage, products (with names), its latest coding-agent builds (status, goal, cost, when; never a preview link) and its hosting on Mynt (status, runtime, last error), if any.

tools.name: admin_get_workspace
tools.title: One workspace, as an admin sees it
tools.description: Admin: one workspace with its members (name, email, role, when they joined), its apps (stage, status, latest build), its invitations (open, accepted, declined or revoked) and its latest activity from the audit log (events about the workspace or its apps, newest first).

tools.name: admin_invite_workspace_member
tools.title: Invite someone to any workspace
tools.description: Admin: invite an email address to any workspace, with an owner's authority (role owner, admin or member; mynt_role developer or user), by the same rules and path as invite_to_workspace: the workspace's organization in the identity provider sends its invitation, a frozen workspace refuses, and they accept it themselves. Audited with by_admin.

tools.name: admin_list_risks
tools.title: Open risks across Mynt
tools.description: Admin: the risks not yet closed on every register (apps', products' and the platform's own), or one kind (subject_type): counts by level (critical, high, medium, low), how many are overdue for review, the total, and the highest-scored risks (score, then the earliest review date), each with its subject's name.

tools.name: admin_pause_campaign
tools.title: Pause any campaign
tools.description: Admin: take any live campaign down now (e.g. a compliance issue). Its developer can fix and relaunch it.

tools.name: admin_remove_workspace_member
tools.title: Remove someone from any workspace
tools.description: Admin: remove a member from any workspace, as remove_workspace_member does for its owners: never its last owner; they leave its organization and lose access to its apps and builds at once.

tools.name: admin_revoke_workspace_invite
tools.title: Withdraw any workspace invite
tools.description: Admin: withdraw an open invite to any workspace (admin_get_workspace lists them), as revoke_workspace_invite does for its owners.

tools.name: admin_set_product_composition
tools.title: Set a reference product's composition
tools.description: Admin: the regulated primitives one of Mynt's reference products (or any product) is made of, per jurisdiction. Reference products name no providers; a firm's product names them from its roster. Its regulatory regime follows (get_product_regime).

key.description: Unique in the product; parties and business context refer to it

primitive.description: The primitive is the line: credit, securitization, payments, account_operations, custody_settlement, wealth, insurance, guarantees_trade, exchange, derivatives or information

action.description: What is done with it in this product: issuance, sale, purchase, secondary_sale, repackaging, advice, servicing, underwriting or assessment (an independent rating, valuation, index, actuarial certification, audit or accreditation)

underlying.description: What it is made of, when the line alone doesn't say: cash, securities, commodities, real_assets, receivables, risk, data or digital_assets

wrapper.description: A statutory or tax structure around it: statutory_pension, tax_advantaged or government_scheme

provider.description: Who provides it. Required on a firm's product; Mynt reference products (no firm) leave it out

licence_id.description: One of your entity's held licences; omit to use whichever covers it (pinned at publish)

party_id.description: An active external party on your entity's roster (see add_party)

entity_id.description: A licence provider's firm id (shared out of band); it covers the component once it approves your request_sponsorship

offered_in.description: Where it's offered, when its country licenses state by state: ISO 3166-2 codes in its country (e.g. ['us-ny', 'us-ca']), or the country code (['us']) for the whole country, which needs a licence covering all of it. Coverage is checked in each. Omit to check the country as a whole, as before

party_id.description: A party on your entity's roster

for.description: The component key it stands behind

tools.name: admin_set_product_status
tools.title: Unpublish or republish any product
tools.description: Admin: unpublish any product (bundled ones included) now, or republish one; republishing runs the product tests against the current reference data and refuses if they fail.

tools.name: adopt_variant
tools.title: Adopt an explored variant
tools.description: Innovator: propose one explorer's variant: Mynt opens a pull request in your workspace with its holdout results. The product doesn't change until you merge it and set the algorithm's new version.

tools.name: analyze_product
tools.title: Analyse a product's feasibility
tools.description: Innovator: work out whether a product makes sense. If a model in your workspace applies, Mynt runs it on the term sheet: code only, no AI, a few cents. If none applies yet and auto_agent is on, the desk agent builds one (intelligence work, within your cap) and Mynt runs that.

model.description: A specific model in your workspace; otherwise the most specific one that applies

cap_usd.description: For the agent, if it's needed

tools.name: app_logs
tools.title: A hosted app's logs
tools.description: Developer: the latest log lines of your hosted app, with timestamps. Secrets are scrubbed.

service.description: For a compose app: the service (e.g. api or web)

tools.name: app_run
tools.title: Run a command in a hosted app
tools.description: Developer: run a shell command inside your hosted app's container (under gVisor, read-only apart from /tmp), e.g. 'node --version' or 'wget -qO- localhost:<your mynt.port>/healthz'. It never runs on the VM itself. Output is capped and secrets are scrubbed; every command is audited.

service.description: For a compose app: the service (e.g. api or web)

tools.name: app_status
tools.title: How a hosted app is doing
tools.description: Developer: your hosted app on your VM, each Compose service (or its one container): running or not, since when, health, how many times it restarted, image (the verified commit), CPU and memory.

tools.name: append_chat_events
tools.title: Add to a chat session
tools.description: Signed-in user: add events to the end of one of your chat sessions, in order: messages (one UI message each; a message appended again under its id replaces the earlier copy when the session is replayed), draft outcomes, a new title. Events are never changed or removed one by one. An event with a client_id the session already has is skipped, so a retried append never adds anything twice. Limits: 100 events per call, 128 KB per event, 1 MB and 5000 events per session.

id.description: The session's id (a UUID the caller picks when it creates the session)

type.description: message: one UI message as the studio has it (its id, role and parts); outcome: what became of a draft; title: { title }; metadata: references merged into the session's metadata; part, draft: kind-specific state

client_id.description: The caller's own id for this event: an append retried with it is never added twice

payload.description: The event itself, as JSON (at most 128 KB)

expect_seq.description: Refuse unless the session still ends at this event number

tools.name: approve_identity_provider
tools.title: Accept an identity provider for a sponsorship
tools.description: Licence provider (for a sponsorship of yours) or admin: accept one identity provider's offering, so the home state it verifies counts for live money movements under this sponsorship. Your own firm's offerings need no approval. A builder's own firm can never be approved for its own product. Audited.

tools.name: approve_mainnet_program
tools.title: Approve a mainnet program
tools.description: Admin: approve a mainnet deploy or upgrade whose automated gates all passed. Name every exception the review lists in allow_exceptions (what can change the build beyond the reviewed source, and crates off the allowlist); approval is refused otherwise. The answer shows the whole report again, with what the gate can't promise. The approval is used once: a first deploy may then go ahead with deploy_program for exactly that build within MAINNET_APPROVAL_TTL_DAYS (default 14); an upgrade runs once its timelock ends. Recorded in the audit log.

note.description: Why it's approved, for the audit log

allow_exceptions.description: The id of every exception the review lists (build scripts, proc macros, cargo config, non-Rust includes, crates off the allowlist...), each one you allow; approval is refused unless all are named

tools.name: approve_partner_kit_change
tools.title: Approve (or decline) a live change another member asked for
tools.description: Licence provider: when your firm has a member who joined before the one asking, a live signing key change or a switch to a live ledger source needs that earlier member's approval. Approve or decline a pending request (its id is in get_partner_kit's pending_approvals and in your notices). Only a member who joined before the requester, and is past the member cool-off, decides it. Approving claims the request, runs the change with every check again, and puts it back if the change fails; a decline can't land while it's being approved. A newer request of the same kind supersedes an older one. Audited.

tools.name: approve_pool
tools.title: Approve a liquidity pool
tools.description: Licence provider: approve a pool on a product your firm sponsors, naming the approved money rails its capital moves on: a deposit rail (direction deposit or on_ramp) and a withdrawal rail (direction payout or off_ramp), both your firm's and approved. Every state the deposit rail serves must also be served by the withdrawal rail, so capital that came in can get out. Deposits and withdrawals are refused without them, and later refused at the chokepoint if a named rail is suspended or revoked: a pool never follows a replacement rail.

tools.name: approve_rail
tools.title: Approve a money rail
tools.description: Admin: approve a proposed rail, or put a suspended one back. Every state must be covered by a verified, in-force licence of the firm that grants money transmission there, with its prerequisites held (the FinCEN registration), or it's refused naming the states outside. Whoever proposed the rail, or belongs to its firm, can't approve it. Audited, with who approved it and when.

tools.name: approve_repository_connection
tools.title: Approve a repository connection
tools.description: Admin: let Mynt give out tokens for this connection. Name it exactly as list_repository_requests showed it (id, repository, installation_id): if it changed since, nothing is approved. Audited; the person who asked is told.

tools.name: approve_sponsorship
tools.title: Sponsor a product under your licences
tools.description: Licence provider: approve a pending request to sponsor a builder's product component, naming the held licences it's under (verified and in force; licences that only back others, like a federal registration a state licence requires, are counted automatically and aren't named) and the jurisdictions you sponsor it in (ISO 3166-2 codes like 'us-ny', or the country code for the whole country; by default those asked for that the licences cover). The component is then covered there only, by your licence, and your roster must fill the stakeholders that licence mandates. Your firm must first pass Mynt's public checks that it's a real company (see get_my_entity's legitimacy). Revoke it later with revoke_sponsorship.

licence_ids.description: Your held licences to sponsor it under (see list_my_licenses)

tools.name: archive_product
tools.title: Archive a financial product
tools.description: Innovator: put one of your products in idea or staging out of the way, with the reason (audited as product_archived). It leaves list_my_products (include_archived shows it) and every build: list_buildable_products, create_app and update_app no longer take it and builds skip it, so a product in staging leaves sandbox builds. It can't be promoted while archived. Nothing is deleted, and its stage is kept: unarchive_product puts it back. A product in production is refused: move it back first (demote_product).

tools.name: archive_workspace
tools.title: Archive a workspace
tools.description: Developer: owners only. Freezes the workspace (nobody new joins) and, 7 days later, removes and offboards everyone and deletes its organization in the identity provider. Until then any owner can undo it with unarchive_workspace. Not while any of its apps is published or hosted: unpublish and undeploy them first. now: true does it at once and can't be undone; only a workspace's sole owner can choose it.

tools.name: audit_log
tools.title: Audit log
tools.description: Admin: recent admin actions, newest first, with who did them and each action's class (security, financial, obligations or workspace).

tools.name: bd_erase
tools.title: Erase a prospect's data
tools.description: Admin: erase everything the connector holds about a person (e.g. a request received elsewhere). By default they also stay suppressed; only the hashes and the reason remain.

tools.name: bd_overview
tools.title: Connector overview
tools.description: Admin: the connector agent's pipeline, today's messages and drafts, channels, spend and caps.

tools.name: bd_pause
tools.title: Pause or resume the connector
tools.description: Admin: the kill switch. Pausing stops any running agent and refuses every message until resumed.

tools.name: bd_prospects
tools.title: Connector prospects
tools.description: Admin: browse the pipeline, or open one prospect with their whole conversation.

tools.name: bd_run_now
tools.title: Run the connector now
tools.description: Admin: start a connector run at the next tick instead of waiting for the schedule.

tools.name: bd_suppress
tools.title: Suppress an address
tools.description: Admin: never contact this email or number again (e.g. a request received elsewhere).

tools.name: block_firm_recovery
tools.title: Block an admin's recovery of a firm's licence provider
tools.description: Anyone who has been a licence provider at a firm, even one whose role has since been taken away: block an admin's recovery (recover_firm_member) of a request at that firm while it waits out its 7 days. The request is declined; it's audited and told to every current and past licence provider of the firm.

tools.name: call_program
tools.title: Call a Solana program
tools.description: Developer: send an instruction to one of your deployed programs. Mynt simulates it first and sends it only if the simulation succeeds, with fees from your own fee payer (never passed to the program) and signed by your caller key only where the instruction lists $caller as a signer; never Mynt's deploy authority. Mainnet is refused until it's configured and enabled.

method.description: An Anchor instruction's name in snake_case (e.g. 'record'); Mynt adds its discriminator

data_base64.description: Instead of method: the whole instruction data, base64 (non-Anchor programs)

pubkey.description: An address, or "$caller" for your caller key (the only signer a call may have; it signs only when listed with signer: true)

instruction.description: The instruction to send to the program

tools.name: cancel_enrollment
tools.title: Cancel an enrollment
tools.description: Consumer: stop using a financial product you are enrolled in.

tools.name: cancel_mainnet_review
tools.title: Cancel a mainnet program review
tools.description: Developer (or admin): cancel a mainnet review that is running, awaiting approval, or approved but not yet started, including a scheduled upgrade during its timelock. The firm's webhooks hear of a cancelled upgrade (program.upgrade_cancelled).

tools.name: cancel_withdrawal
tools.title: Cancel a withdrawal request
tools.description: Liquidity provider: leave the queue with one of your requests. Anything already on its way carries on; only the rest is cancelled. A fully-claimed request (paying) can't be cancelled; a parked one can.

tools.name: change_member_role
tools.title: Change a member's role
tools.description: Developer: owners and admins change a member's role. Only owners make or unmake owners, and a workspace always keeps at least one owner.

tools.name: check_experience
tools.title: Check an experience against the products' terms
tools.description: Developer: for one of your apps, whether you have access to each product and whether the experience meets each product's build terms (permitted actions, required disclosures, banned wording), plus structural checks of its experience definition (see set_experience). All must pass to publish.

tools.name: check_journey
tools.title: Check a journey
tools.description: Developer: check a journey spec against its product's live developer contract, on every path: consent before personal data, the product's documents before any hosted action, every field an action needs collected before it and none it doesn't need, sensitive fields only in secure inputs, every step reachable and every path ending. Errors name the step and the fix; paths lists every route through it for simulation.

tools.name: check_module
tools.title: Check a module manifest
tools.description: Developer: check a module's manifest against the live developer contracts it's built on: the actions exist and may run where the module runs (client: client actions; server: any; isomorphic: only actions that run either side), it declares every consent those actions need, and a client component renders every document its products require.

tools.name: check_product_definition
tools.title: Check a v2 product definition
tools.description: Validate a v2 product definition (its JSON Schema is the resource mynt://schemas/financial-product.v2) without saving it: the JSON Schema; that every connection end resolves (components, segments, algorithms, risk models, handoffs, terms… and upstream: the owner's licences, roster parties, register personas and items, current GRC records); and the composition rules (allowed primitive × action at each end of funds, converts_into, guarantees, discovers_price_for and the other links; one provider per component; a handoff to each providing party; one primary risk model per algorithm; every risk model governed). Pass product_id to check it against that product's firm; a valid definition then also lists publish_blockers, what its regime would refuse at publish (an uncovered component, a mandated stakeholder missing or not bound to its component).

tools.name: close_agreement_audit
tools.title: Pass, fail or waive an oversight audit
tools.description: Licence provider: close an open audit of an agreement with your firm. passed: only once the app's side has submitted evidence and every finding is resolved. failed or waived: at any point, with a note saying why. Mynt opens the requirement's next audit when its time comes. Audited; the app's side is told.

tools.name: close_program
tools.title: Close a devnet program
tools.description: Admin: close a deployed devnet program for good, with the upgradeable loader's Close on its program data, signed by Mynt's devnet deploy authority; the program data's lamports go back to that authority. The program can never run or be deployed again, and its record is marked closed. Refused on mainnet: Mynt never closes a mainnet program.

tools.name: close_sandbox
tools.title: Close a reopened sandbox
tools.description: Developer: end the sandbox you reopened on a build's branch (anything not pushed is lost).

tools.name: commit_to_pool
tools.title: Commit capital to a pool
tools.description: Liquidity provider: commit capital to a pool. This asks for a deposit, in integer cents, on the pool's approved rail; your position counts only what has settled. Real (non-sandbox) commitments are refused until an admin records that the pool's offering was cleared and on what legal basis, because pooled investor capital with withdrawal rights may be a securities offering. Mynt never holds your funds. state: the US state your capital moves from, which the rail must serve.

idempotency_key.description: A key you choose for this one action: repeating a call with the same key is the same action, not a second one

tools.name: configure_partner_ledger
tools.title: Propose a licence provider's ledger endpoints
tools.description: Admin: propose a licence provider's test and live HTTPS endpoints for its ledger feed (Mynt POSTs to <url>/v1/ledger). An origin and a path only: HTTPS on 443, public addresses, no query string or fragment, and different from each other. Nothing changes until the firm's own licence provider confirms them (confirm_partner_ledger_endpoints); the firm is told on its webhooks. Audited.

tools.name: configure_solana_signer
tools.title: Configure the Solana mainnet signer
tools.description: Admin: choose who signs Mynt's mainnet deploys and upgrades, and turn mainnet on or off. Backends: mainnet-vault (a key in Mynt's vault; the server must also set SOLANA_MAINNET_VAULT_SIGNER=enabled), custody-service (Turnkey signs each transaction with a Solana wallet account it holds; Mynt never sees the key, and the server must set TURNKEY_ORGANIZATION_ID, TURNKEY_API_PUBLIC_KEY and TURNKEY_API_PRIVATE_KEY), multisig (Squads-style; members approve each change). Mainnet stays refused until the backend is ready and enabled is true. Call with no arguments to see the current state and what's missing.

generate_key.description: mainnet-vault: generate the mainnet key in Mynt's vault (only its address is ever shown)

custody_provider.description: custody-service: the provider that holds the key (default turnkey)

custody_address.description: custody-service: the Solana wallet account address the provider signs with (Turnkey's signWith)

multisig_vault.description: multisig: the vault address that holds the upgrade authority

tools.name: configure_treasury_mainnet
tools.title: Treasury mainnet: readiness, and the switch
tools.description: Admin: with no arguments, whether treasury mainnet is on and whether this server is ready for it (a mainnet RPC, SOLANA_RPC_URL_MAINNET, checked against mainnet's genesis hash; and the vault for Mynt's mainnet attester), with what's missing. enabled: true turns it on, only when ready (mainnet_not_ready otherwise); enabled: false turns it off at once. While it's on, pools passing every mainnet check can be registered on mainnet and take real USDC deposits; turning it off stops every mainnet deposit and approval, and withdrawal requests still go through. Recorded in the audit log.

tools.name: confirm_partner_ledger_endpoints
tools.title: Confirm (or decline) the ledger endpoints an admin proposed
tools.description: Licence provider: an admin's proposed test and live endpoints (get_partner_kit, pending_endpoint_change) take effect only when you confirm them. Check both are your own deployments, then pass them back exactly. Confirming a change puts your firm back on the sandbox until it passes conformance again. accept: false declines it. Audited.

tools.name: connect_answer_intro
tools.title: Answer an introduction
tools.description: Say yes or no to meeting someone the connector suggested.

tools.name: connect_desk_repository
tools.title: Connect your desk workspace
tools.description: Innovator: connect your firm's GitHub repository as its product-desk workspace (install the Mynt GitHub App on it first). Your financial models live there as code; Mynt runs them, and the desk agent proposes new ones as pull requests.

tools.name: connect_forget_me
tools.title: Forget me
tools.description: Erase everything Mynt's connector holds about you (profile, messages, introductions, consents), and never contact you again. Your Mynt account itself isn't affected.

tools.name: connect_my_intros
tools.title: My introductions
tools.description: Introductions Mynt's connector has proposed for you; answer them with connect_answer_intro.

tools.name: connect_refer
tools.title: Refer someone to Mynt
tools.description: Point Mynt's connector to someone who should be on Mynt (an innovator or a developer). It will reach out once by email, saying you referred them only if you allow it.

tools.name: connect_repository
tools.title: Connect a GitHub repository for builds
tools.description: Developer: let Mynt's coding agent push branches and open pull requests on one of your repositories. Install the Mynt GitHub App on it first (the result tells you where). If the GitHub account linked to your sign-in can push to it (admin, maintain or write), it's approved at once; otherwise an admin approves it, and the result says why (link your GitHub account at manage_url to skip that).

tools.name: connect_with_mynt
tools.title: Talk to Mynt's connector
tools.description: Tell Mynt's connector (an AI agent) what you do and what you're looking for: an innovator bringing financial products, or a developer building on them. It introduces you to the right people, with your yes first. Give WhatsApp or a phone number only if you'd like to be reached there.

about.description: What you or your firm does: licences, products, stack, customers

looking_for.description: Who you'd like to meet, or what you need

phone.description: For a call, if you'd like one

tools.name: create_api_key
tools.title: Create an API key for an app
tools.description: Developer: a key your app uses to call Mynt's runtime API (/v1). live keys (mynt_live_…) work once the app is published; sandbox keys (mynt_test_…) work on drafts and simulate hand-offs. The key is shown once; Mynt keeps only its hash. List allowed_origins to call the API from browsers on those origins.

allowed_origins.description: Browser origins allowed to use this key (CORS); empty: server-side only

tools.name: create_app
tools.title: Create an app experience
tools.description: Developer: create a draft app experience (e.g. a retirement planner or first-salary starter kit) on published products, in one of your workspaces (everyone in it can work on it). Declare what it does (actions) and the disclosures it shows; check_experience tells you whether it meets each product's terms.

workspace_id.description: The workspace it belongs to (list_workspaces). Omitted: the workspace you created, or a new one of your own if you created none

audience.description: Who the experience is for, e.g. 'first-time investors in India'

disclosures.description: Text the experience shows users, e.g. risk warnings the products require

actions.description: What the experience does with the products (default: display)

tools.name: create_app_idea
tools.title: Add an app idea
tools.description: Admin: add a specific app idea on an app kind, offered on New app. Its chip_label is the chip's short label (1 to 34 characters on one line, plain words saying what the app is), the problem is a plain problem statement (who, and the problem) shown as the chip's tooltip, the pitch says what the app does about it, and the goal is where the build starts. Refused if the kind isn't there, a line or category isn't the kind's, the text is about lending, insurance, investing, trading or cards, promises or projects earnings, yields, returns or guarantees, gives advice ('not advice' is fine), or frames users as sellers of goods. Factual words about the products (interest, rate, matures, retirement, fund) are fine.

id.description: A short slug, unique across every idea

chip_label.description: The chip's label on the Build page: 1 to 34 characters on one line, plain words saying what the app is ("Two-key household fund"). The problem is the chip's tooltip

problem.description: The problem: who has the problem and what it is, in plain words ("Roommates chase each other for their share of rent and bills"). No product names

pitch.description: One line: what the app does about the problem

goal.description: The goal the build starts from, which the developer edits

product_lines.description: Some or all of the kind's product lines

categories.description: Optional: the product categories in those lines the idea is for (deposits, retirement, ...; within the kind's own, if it lists some). The studio picks the published products in them

product_names.description: Optional: words from the names of the products it's for ("Money Market Account"), when a category is still too wide. The studio picks the published products in the idea's lines and categories whose names contain one

sort.description: Order within the kind, lowest first (default 0)

tools.name: create_campaign
tools.title: Create a campaign
tools.description: Developer (GTM): a draft go-to-market campaign for published products, aimed at a segment (or everyone), on chosen channels, with one or more copy variants for A/B testing. Lint, then launch.

tools.name: create_chat_session
tools.title: Start a chat session
tools.description: Signed-in user: keep one of your studio chats on Mynt (a financial-product chat, an Earn chat), under an id you pick. Creating it again with the same id answers the one you have. Only you can read it. You keep at most 200 of each kind: a new one past that deletes your oldest of that kind.

id.description: The session's id (a UUID the caller picks when it creates the session)

workspace_id.description: The workspace the chat was had in, if any (you must be a member)

metadata.description: Small references only: a product id, pool ids

tools.name: create_entity
tools.title: Register your firm
tools.description: Innovator: register the legal entity you act for (once), as typed facts: legal form, incorporation (lowercase ISO codes, e.g. { country: 'in', subdivision: 'in-mh' }) and identifiers ({ scheme: 'in_cin' | 'lei' | …, value }). Its licences, or a licence provider's sponsorship (request_sponsorship), let you publish products; its party roster (add_party) says who stands behind them.

tools.name: create_firm_webhook
tools.title: Receive your vendor services' results
tools.description: Innovator: an https URL where Mynt sends your firm the full result of every client action a product's bound vendor service answered (vendor_action.completed, with data.result) or that failed (vendor_action.failed), so your firm acts on it; apps' devices only get a status. It also gets your Solana programs' deploys, upgrades and events (program.deployed, program.upgraded, program.event), and, for a licence provider, its covenants' alerts on the products it sponsors (covenant.breached, covenant.cleared). Each POST carries Mynt-Signature (t=<unix>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "t.body" with the secret>). The secret is shown once.

events.description: Every event your role may receive, by default

tools.name: create_pool
tools.title: Create a liquidity pool for a product
tools.description: Builder: propose a pool that liquidity providers can put capital into, on a product of your firm whose component is sponsored by an approved licence provider (with no approved sponsorship, it's refused). A minimum reserve (basis points of the pool's obligations plus a floor in cents), a notice period in days (0 allowed), and per-firm commitment limits in cents. Sandbox pools move no real money. The sponsor must approve it (approve_pool) and name its rails before it can take commitments.

component_key.description: The sponsored component this pool serves

min_reserve_bps.description: Minimum reserve as basis points of obligations, 10000 = 100%

min_commitment_cents.description: A firm's smallest total position in this pool, integer cents

max_commitment_cents.description: A firm's largest total position in this pool, integer cents

sponsor_entity_id.description: If more than one licence provider sponsors the component

idempotency_key.description: Optional: a key you choose for this proposal. Repeating the call with the same key and the same arguments returns the pool made the first time, not a second one; the same key with different arguments is refused

tools.name: create_product
tools.title: Create a financial product
tools.description: Innovator: create a draft financial product. action says what your firm does with it: issuance (you are the issuer), sale (you distribute another issuer's products, e.g. as a mutual fund distributor) or repackaging (you bundle others' products, e.g. a model portfolio); for sale and repackaging name the underlying products. Publishing needs a verified licence covering that action: your firm's, or, for a composed product, a licence provider's that sponsors a component (request_sponsorship). Run test_product, then publish_product.

category.description: A category admins have defined for this product line (see list_product_categories)

region.description: A region admins have defined: 'global' or a country code such as IN (see list_regions)

underlying_product_ids.description: For sale or repackaging: the published products this builds on

tools.name: create_product_idea
tools.title: Add a financial product idea
tools.description: Admin: add an idea for a new financial product, offered in the Build page's Financial product mode, with a chip_label of 1 to 34 characters for its chip. Refused if its region, product line or category has no products Mynt runs there (US: account_operations/deposits, wealth/retirement, wealth/mutual_funds, credit/bonds), if any text promises, projects or advises (earnings, yields, returns, a percentage, guarantees, 'risk-free', beating inflation, recommendations, advice), frames the people it serves as sellers of goods, or is about lending, insurance or crypto.

id.description: A short slug, unique across product ideas

chip_label.description: The chip's label on the Build page: 1 to 34 characters on one line, plain words, usually a shortened product name ("Goal-locked savings pots"). The product name and label are the chip's tooltip

label.description: The label: who needs the product and what for, in plain words ("Gig workers with uneven pay can't lock cash away for months")

product_name.description: A draft name for the product, which the firm edits

summary.description: One line: what the product is, factually

product_line.description: A product line with products in the region

category.description: A category in that line with products in the region (deposits, retirement, mutual_funds, bonds)

region.description: The region Mynt launches products in

key_features.description: The product's key features, each one line, stated as terms the firm sets

risk_level.description: Optional: prefilled in the Create product sheet

liquidity.description: Optional: prefilled in the Create product sheet

typical_horizon.description: Optional: prefilled in the Create product sheet

return_type.description: Optional: prefilled in the Create product sheet

sort.description: Order within the product line, lowest first (default 0)

tools.name: create_product_version
tools.title: Draft a new version of a product
tools.description: Innovator: start the next version of one of your published products from its live version, with a changelog. Fields you pass change; then test_product and publish_product. The live version keeps serving until then.

changelog.description: What changes for customers in this version

category.description: A category admins have defined for this product line (see list_product_categories)

region.description: A region admins have defined: 'global' or a country code such as IN (see list_regions)

tools.name: create_sdk
tools.title: Create an SDK
tools.description: Developer: define an SDK over products you can build on (open or approval products, or ones you've been let into). generate_sdk_release then produces a versioned bundle: an OpenAPI 3.1 document and typed TypeScript and/or Python clients for the Mynt app API.

tools.name: create_segment
tools.title: Create an audience segment
tools.description: Developer (GTM): define an audience from consumers' current enrollments, e.g. holders of a savings product without term insurance.

enrolled_in.description: Consumers active in any of these product ids

enrolled_in_lines.description: Consumers active in any product of these lines

not_enrolled_in.description: Consumers active in none of these product ids (e.g. to cross-sell)

tools.name: create_test_consumer
tools.title: Create a sandbox test consumer
tools.description: Developer: an opaque consumer_ref to use as a test user in sandbox hand-offs. It identifies nobody and carries no personal or financial data.

tools.name: create_vendor_offering
tools.title: Offer a standard service
tools.description: Vendor: offer a standard service type in a region from your test (and live) HTTPS endpoint, with your per-call price and the licences you hold for it, and your standard terms (standard_terms: the document link (https) and its SHA-256, a short summary and your pricing in words; you bill subscribers directly). Listing an offering with terms is your standing acceptance of them: app workspaces subscribe by accepting them in the marketplace, with no negotiation. It starts as a draft: run_conformance, then update_vendor_offering { listed: true }. The conformance signing secret is shown once.

test_base_url.description: HTTPS base URL of your test endpoint; Mynt calls POST <base>/v1/<service_type>

live_base_url.description: HTTPS base URL of your live endpoint

price.description: Your fixed price per call, for innovators to see; billing is between you and them, not through Mynt

licence_ids.description: Licences your firm holds (get_my_entity) that this offering relies on

requires_credential.description: true when subscribers must give Mynt a credential you issue them; it's sent as Authorization: Bearer

summary.description: The terms in a few sentences, as subscribers see them before accepting

pricing_summary.description: Your pricing in words (e.g. '$0.40 per check, invoiced monthly'); you bill subscribers directly, never through Mynt

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.title: Register a webhook
tools.description: Developer: receive events about one of your apps' products at an https URL: product.version_published, product.unpublished, product.suspended, product.drifted, product.drift_cleared, access.approved, access.revoked, request.decided, handoff.completed, handoff.failed, handoff.reversed (a completed Mynt Ramp transfer the bank later sent back). Each POST carries a Mynt-Signature header (t=<unix>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "t.body" with the secret>). The secret is shown once.

tools.name: create_workspace
tools.title: Create a workspace
tools.description: Developer: a new workspace for a team's apps. You're its owner; invite_to_workspace brings others in.

tools.name: decide_firm_member
tools.title: Accept (or decline) an account an admin added to your firm
tools.description: Licence provider: an account an admin adds to your firm, when it already has licence-provider members, waits for one of you to accept it. Until then it's a member of nothing; once accepted it joins, and its member cool-off starts then. Declining ends the request. Pending ones are in get_partner_kit (pending_members) and your notices. Audited.

tools.name: decide_promotion_signoff
tools.title: Approve or reject a production sign-off
tools.description: Admin: approve or reject a sign-off request, with a note. Only for the build it was asked for while that is still the app's latest verified build; never one you asked for yourself. Recorded in the audit trail.

tools.name: decide_review_case
tools.title: Decide a governance review
tools.description: Admin: your decision on a ready case. For a licence, verify or reject sets its review status (as review_license does); needs_info records it and changes nothing. Recorded in the audit log with Mynt's recommendation.

tools.name: decline_sponsorship
tools.title: Decline to sponsor a product
tools.description: Licence provider: decline a pending request to sponsor a builder's product component, saying why.

tools.name: decline_workspace_invite
tools.title: Decline a workspace invitation
tools.description: Decline an invitation to a workspace (list_my_invitations).

tools.name: define_judgment
tools.title: Define a judgment
tools.description: Admin: add or replace a court or tribunal decision in a region: case name, court and level, citation, date, bench, holding, the legislation it interprets, whether it is still good law, official URL and what it applies to. Obligations and filings can cite it by id (legal_ref).

title.description: Case name, e.g. 'X v. Union of India'

court.description: e.g. Supreme Court of India, Securities Appellate Tribunal

citation.description: e.g. a law-report citation or case number

holding.description: The legal principle the court decided

tools.name: define_legal_instrument
tools.title: Define a legal instrument (deprecated)
tools.description: Deprecated: use define_legislation or define_judgment. Files kind 'judgment' under the judiciary and everything else under legislation.

citation.description: e.g. 'Act No. 2 of 1934' or a circular number

issued_by.description: Regulator id, or the legislature (e.g. parliament)

tools.name: define_legislation
tools.title: Define legislation
tools.description: Admin: add or replace a legislative instrument in a region (act, ordinance, rule, regulation, master direction, circular, guideline, notification, order) with its citation, issuer, the instrument it is made under, effective date, status, official URL, summary and what it applies to. Obligations and filings cite it by id (legal_ref).

citation.description: e.g. 'Act No. 2 of 1934' or a circular number

issued_by.description: Regulator id, or the legislature (e.g. parliament)

parent_id.description: The legislative id this is made under, e.g. the act a rule or direction derives from

tools.name: define_product_category
tools.title: Define a product category
tools.description: Admin: add or change a product type and the product lines it can be used in. Lines are by economic function, not asset class: credit, securitization, payments, account_operations, custody_settlement, wealth, insurance, guarantees_trade, exchange, derivatives, information. A category can sit in several (e.g. exchange_traded: wealth and securitization). Set active=false to retire it for new products.

tools.name: define_region
tools.title: Define a region
tools.description: Admin: add or change a geography products may be offered in: its regulators, regulatory ecosystem, the legal procedure to launch each product line there, and the official sources. Fields you leave out keep their current value. Set active=false to stop new products using it (live products stay).

regulators.description: Short names of the regulators products here answer to, e.g. RBI, SEBI, IRDAI. test_product checks a product's regulator against these.

ecosystem.description: Markdown overview: each regulator's remit, the key laws and regulations, self-regulatory bodies, and how they interact

procedures.description: How each product line (credit, securitization, payments, account_operations, custody_settlement, wealth, insurance, guarantees_trade, exchange, derivatives, information) is legally brought to market here. Replaces the region's whole list when given.

steps.description: Licences, registrations, approvals and filings, in order

sources.description: Official regulator or statute pages the content is drawn from

tools.name: define_regulated_product_type
tools.title: Define a regulated product type
tools.description: Admin: add or replace a product type in a region's regulated product catalogue (e.g. term deposit, listed NCD, ULIP): its Mynt category, every action that can be taken on it (issuance, sale, purchase, secondary_sale, repackaging, advice, servicing, underwriting, assessment; assessment is an independent rating, valuation, index, actuarial certification, audit or accreditation), and optionally its underlying (what it is made of) and wrapper (a statutory pension, tax-advantaged or government-scheme structure around it). Product types live apart from regulators; each regulator then maps the ones it supervises (define_regulator scope.product_types), so one product type can sit under several regulators. Narrowing actions is refused while a regulator still supervises the dropped ones.

type_id.description: The Mynt product category this maps to (see list_product_categories)

actions.description: Every action that can be taken on this product type

underlying.description: What it is made of: cash, securities, commodities, real_assets, receivables, risk, data or digital_assets

wrapper.description: A statutory or tax structure around it: statutory_pension, tax_advantaged or government_scheme

tools.name: define_regulator
tools.title: Define a regulator
tools.description: Admin: add or replace one regulator in a region's regulatory model: the regulated product types it supervises (ids from the region's catalogue, see define_regulated_product_type, each with the actions it supervises), customer personas and their qualifications, and the licences it grants, each with its GRC (obligations, filings, risks, controls, repositories, the product types and actions it grants, allowed segments, mandatory internal and external stakeholders). Persona and licence ids must start with '<regulator id>_' and can't be used by another regulator in the region. Broken links are refused; links to law not yet recorded come back as warnings.

short_name.description: How products cite it, e.g. RBI

jurisdiction.description: A sub-national regulator's jurisdiction, as an ISO 3166-2 code in the region's country (e.g. 'us-ny' for a New York regulator). Omit for a national regulator: its licences cover the whole country

product_types.description: Regulated product types this regulator supervises; define them first with define_regulated_product_type

id.description: A regulated product type id in this region (see list_regulated_product_types)

actions.description: The actions this regulator supervises; a subset of the product type's actions. Omit for all of them.

qualification.description: Criteria as key/value pairs, e.g. { min_net_worth_inr: 50000000, resident: true }

covers.description: Where a held licence of this type lets its holder provide what it grants: ISO 3166-2 codes ('us-ny'), or the country code for the whole country ('us', e.g. a federal charter that pre-empts state licensing for the activities it grants). Omit for the regulator's jurisdiction (its state, or the whole country). An empty list covers nowhere by itself: a registration other licences require (see requires) that licenses nothing on its own, e.g. a federal money services business registration where each state licenses money transmission

requires.description: Licence types (their _ids, in this region) the holder must also hold, verified and in force, for a held licence of this type to count: e.g. a state money transmitter licence requires the federal money services business registration. Each entry is one _id, or a list of _ids any one of which will do (the same registration modelled under different ids). The regime checks it wherever this licence would cover a component, and pins the prerequisite at publish with it

issued_per_jurisdiction.description: True when one licence type is issued separately for each jurisdiction in covers (e.g. a money transmitter licence held in several states): each held licence then records the jurisdiction it was issued for, and covers only that one

coverage_note.description: The basis for covers, e.g. a pre-emption claim, and anything about it still to verify

application_procedure.description: How to obtain the licence, in order

frequency_note.description: Cadence detail the vocabulary can't express

risk_ref.description: Risk id in this licence's risks register

owner.description: Mandatory stakeholder id accountable for it

legal_ref.description: Id of the legislation or judgment it comes from

due.description: Due-date rule, e.g. 'within 30 days of quarter end'

control_test_frequency.description: How often controls over this risk must be tested

guidance.description: How the regulator expects licensees to define and run this

legal_ref.description: Legislation or judgment id that mandates it

extends_default.description: Start from Mynt's default field schema for this kind

fields.description: Fields added to (or overriding, by key) the default schema

mitigates.description: Risk ids in this licence's risks register

owner.description: Mandatory stakeholder id who owns the control

guidance.description: How the regulator expects licensees to define and run this

legal_ref.description: Legislation or judgment id that mandates it

fields.description: Fields added to (or overriding, by key) the default schema

guidance.description: How the regulator expects licensees to define and run this

legal_ref.description: Legislation or judgment id that mandates it

extends_default.description: Start from Mynt's default field schema for this kind

fields.description: Fields added to (or overriding, by key) the default schema

approved_by.description: Stakeholder id that must approve it, e.g. the board

guidance.description: How the regulator expects licensees to define and run this

legal_ref.description: Legislation or judgment id that mandates it

extends_default.description: Start from Mynt's default field schema for this kind

fields.description: Fields added to (or overriding, by key) the default schema

guidance.description: How the regulator expects licensees to define and run this

legal_ref.description: Legislation or judgment id that mandates it

extends_default.description: Start from Mynt's default field schema for this kind

fields.description: Fields added to (or overriding, by key) the default schema

allowed_product_types.description: Product types from this regulator's scope.product_types, each with the actions this licence permits

actions.description: The actions this licence permits; a subset of what the regulator supervises. Omit for all of them.

qualification.description: Criteria as key/value pairs, e.g. { min_net_worth_inr: 50000000, resident: true }

obligations.description: Obligation ids from this licence's register, or short descriptions

qualification.description: Criteria as key/value pairs, e.g. { min_net_worth_inr: 50000000, resident: true }

obligations.description: Obligation ids from this licence's register, or short descriptions

guidance.description: What the regulator expects here, in plain words

reference_to.description: What a reference points at: risk, obligation, stakeholder, legal, policy, control, regulator, file

fields.description: For object fields and arrays of objects

tools.name: define_service_type
tools.title: Define a standard service
tools.description: Admin: add or replace a standard service type in a region: the input and output JSON Schemas every vendor implements, the consent purpose, the data dictionary fields its output fills, and the licence types (from the region's regulatory model) the subscribing firm and the vendor must hold.

key.description: Unique in the region; vendors serve it at POST <base>/v1/<key>

input_schema.description: JSON Schema of `input`. Required properties must be data dictionary fields: Mynt sends them from the customer's vault

consent_purpose.description: The consent purpose the customer must give first; a handoff bound to this service uses it

fills.description: Data dictionary fields the output fills (output properties of the same name), saved to the customer's vault

innovator_licences.description: Licence type ids (regulatory model) the subscribing firm must hold one of; empty for none

vendor_licences.description: Licence type ids the vendor must hold one of; empty for none

fixtures.description: Inputs for Mynt's conformance test; by default one built from Mynt's sandbox fixtures

client_result.description: What a device that starts an action served by this service is told. The full output goes to the innovator; by default the device gets only a status and a reference

map.description: Its values → the status the device sees; others are 'completed'

fields.description: Output properties the device may see; never personal data

redirect.description: true for services the customer finishes on the provider's page (e-sign, e-mandate, DigiLocker): the device gets the vendor's redirect_url

params_schema.description: JSON Schema of `params`: what the device sends with each call (an amount, a currency, an asset), never customer data, which comes from the vault. An object of plain scalar properties with additionalProperties false

params_fixture.description: params for Mynt's conformance test; needed when params_schema has required properties

quote.description: true for a price quote: its output must require quote_id (string) and expires_at (date-time, at most an hour ahead). The device is shown expires_at and accepts the quote through the service type whose `accepts` names this one

moves_money.description: Required. true for a service that instructs a money movement (every non-quote ramp service): it then runs only through an approved money rail

accepts.description: The key of the quote service type (same region) this service executes. The device sends the quote's reference; Mynt sends the vendor its quote_id, once, only while it hasn't expired, and only to the vendor that quoted

tools.name: define_take_rate
tools.title: Define a take rate
tools.description: Admin: set what Mynt takes on a product line, proportional to each product's compliance and back-office workload: rate = base_pct + workload_pct × workload score, kept between min_pct and max_pct, applied to basis (e.g. revenue or volume). Replaces the line's current rate.

base_pct.description: Percentage taken on every product in the line

workload_pct.description: Percentage added per workload point (see get_product_take_rate)

basis.description: What the percentage applies to, e.g. 'revenue' or 'volume'

tools.name: delete_chat_session
tools.title: Delete a chat session
tools.description: Signed-in user: delete one of your chat sessions and every event in it, for good.

id.description: The session's id (a UUID the caller picks when it creates the session)

tools.name: delete_covenant
tools.title: Delete a covenant
tools.description: Licence provider: remove a rule. A rule that's holding the product paused has to be released first; one with an open breach needs a reason, recorded with the breach. Breaches already recorded stay.

tools.name: delete_firm_webhook
tools.title: Delete a firm webhook
tools.description: Innovator: stop sending vendor service results to one of your firm's webhooks, and drop its delivery history.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.title: Delete a webhook
tools.description: Developer: stop sending events to a webhook, and drop its delivery history.

tools.name: demote_app
tools.title: Move an app down one stage
tools.description: Developer (the workspace's owners and admins): move an app down one stage (production → staging, staging → idea), with the reason, recorded in the workspace's audit trail (app_demoted). Out of production nothing may reach real money: demoting a production app is refused while it has active live keys (revoke them first with revoke_api_key; demotion never revokes them for you), and it unpublishes the app. Its hosting and webhooks stay as they are.

tools.name: demote_product
tools.title: Move a financial product down one stage
tools.description: Innovator: move one of your products down one stage (production → staging, staging → idea), with the reason, recorded in the audit trail (product_demoted). Out of production it leaves the catalogue as unpublish_product does (existing enrollments are kept, no new ones; products built on it pause their sales) and stays open to sandbox builds; out of staging, sandbox builds can no longer pick it.

tools.name: deploy_app
tools.title: Host an app
tools.description: Developer: run one of your apps on its own VM from a build Mynt verified (build_id from your coding-agent builds). The VM fetches exactly that commit, builds it and runs it; each Compose service listens on the port its mynt.port label names and is served publicly over HTTPS. Mynt gives the app a dedicated key (live once the app is in Production and published, else sandbox), added at the edge to its calls to Mynt and never stored on the VM. Deploying again with a newer build replaces it.

tools.name: deploy_program
tools.title: Deploy a Solana program
tools.description: Developer: deploy a reserved program from a build Mynt verified. Mynt deploys the program it built itself in its clean verify sandbox (Anchor's verifiable build, tested on a local validator), never the coding agent's file, and records its hash. Devnet signs with Mynt's devnet key; mainnet is refused until an admin configures and enables the mainnet signer, and needs an approved mainnet review of exactly this build's program (request_mainnet_review). On devnet, `warnings` lists what mainnet's program gate would refuse in the build's source (for example anchor-lang's lazy-account feature, advisory GHSA-6px8-6mw3-4hx4). Runs in the background: follow it with get_program.

build_id.description: A succeeded build whose verification built this program

tools.name: desk_task
tools.title: Give the desk agent a task
tools.description: Innovator: intelligence-driven work for the desk agent in your workspace: design or extend a model (e.g. 'add an ALM liquidity ladder for our FD book', 'model IRDAI commission caps'), stress scenarios, or a shared library. It writes code and tests on a branch; Mynt runs the code and opens a pull request.

tools.name: diff_product_versions
tools.title: Compare two versions
tools.description: Innovator: the fields that differ between two versions of one of your products.

tools.name: download_agreement_document
tools.title: Download a signed agreement
tools.description: Either party's members (the app's workspace, or the other firm): the signed copy of a program agreement Mynt holds (part 'signed'), or the e-signature service's audit certificate with it (part 'certificate'), as base64 with its SHA-256, checked against what Mynt recorded when it was signed. Audited.

tools.name: enable_webhook
tools.title: Turn a disabled webhook back on
tools.description: Developer (the workspace's owners and admins): a webhook stops when the person who made it leaves the workspace, since its address may be theirs. Turning it back on takes its URL: the one it has (list_webhooks shows it), to confirm it's still the right receiver, or a new one. It gets a new signing secret, shown once to you.

url.description: The address deliveries go to: its current one to confirm it, or a new one

tools.name: end_campaign
tools.title: End a campaign
tools.description: Developer (GTM): stop a campaign for good; its metrics stay.

tools.name: end_party
tools.title: End a party's role at your firm
tools.description: Record that a party no longer fills its role at your firm (a person left, an agreement ended). Parties aren't edited: to change one, end it and add the new one. Published products bound to it drift and pause new sales until a new version is published.

tools.name: enroll_in_product
tools.title: Enroll in a financial product
tools.description: Consumer: start using a published financial product (open, subscribe, apply or invest), on its live version. Pass campaign_id when enrolling from an offer in list_offers.

amount.description: Amount to invest, deposit or borrow, if relevant

campaign_id.description: The offer you are responding to, from list_offers

tools.name: file_grc_record
tools.title: File a record in your GRC folder
tools.description: Innovator: file a record in your entity's GRC folder, or in a party's folder (party_id), laid out like the GRC of the licences you hold. Registers: obligations (compliance status, owner party), reporting_disclosure_filings (period, status, filed_on), risks (inherent and residual rating), controls and inspection_events (records following the licence's template fields). Repositories: regulatory_communications, enforcement_actions and press_releases ({ title, date, url, summary }), and policies, risk_models and inspection_history (following the template fields). Records answering the regulator name licence_id and ref (the obligation, filing, risk or template id; see get_regulator). Owners and approvers must be active parties on your roster. Filing the same key again supersedes the current record; history is kept.

party_id.description: File it in a party's folder instead of the entity's

product_id.description: File it in one of your products' folders (e.g. the governance of its risk models)

licence_id.description: The held licence whose GRC item it answers

ref.description: The item in that licence's GRC it answers: an obligation, filing or risk id, or a template id

key.description: Your id for the record (a template can have several records); defaults to ref

tools.name: find_licenses
tools.title: Which licence do I need?
tools.description: Licences in a region that permit an action (issuance, sale, purchase, secondary_sale, repackaging, advice, servicing, underwriting, assessment) on a product category for a customer persona, with the application steps, mandatory stakeholders and filings each brings.

category.description: A Mynt product category id, e.g. deposits

persona.description: A customer persona id from get_regulator

product_type.description: A regulated product type id from list_regulated_product_types

tools.name: finish_build
tools.title: Finish a session build and ship it
tools.description: Developer: end a session build (start_build with mode 'session'). Once its current request is done, the agent reviews, checks, previews and pushes the work, then Mynt verifies it in a clean sandbox exactly as any build: only that verification decides whether it ships. Follow it with get_build.

tools.name: generate_sdk_release
tools.title: Generate an SDK release
tools.description: Developer: generate an immutable, versioned release of one of your SDKs from the products' current published versions and build terms: openapi.json plus typed clients (required disclosures and branding included as constants). Versions are semver and must increase.

tools.name: get_agreement_audit
tools.title: An oversight audit
tools.description: One oversight audit under an app agreement you're a party to: its requirement, due date, status, whether it's overdue, findings (with the app side's answers), evidence (links with their SHA-256), its history (every change, who made it and when) and what you may do next (actions).

tools.name: get_agreement_signing_link
tools.title: Sign a program agreement
tools.description: The signer on either side of an accepted program agreement (who accepted it for the licence provider, who proposed it for the app): a link to sign it inside Mynt Studio (an embedded signing page, valid for a short while; ask again for a fresh one). Mynt makes the e-signature document from the licence provider's active template the first time if it wasn't made when the agreement was accepted, and reads its state back from the e-signature service. The agreement is signed only once the service reports both signatures complete.

tools.name: get_app_customers
tools.title: An app's target customers
tools.description: Developer: the customer segments (personas) each of the app's products declares, which of them the app targets (set_app_target_segments), and how many customers it has where Mynt measures that: distinct customers with client sessions and with records in the customer vault, live and sandbox apart. A count Mynt can't measure yet (no client sessions in that environment) is null with the reason, never 0.

tools.name: get_app_metrics
tools.title: App analytics
tools.description: Developer: views, clicks and hand-offs (started, completed, failed) for one of your apps, with conversion (completed hand-offs per view), per product and per day. Live traffic only unless include_sandbox. handoff_events counts the handoff_started events your app reported; handoffs_* count hand-offs made through POST /v1/handoffs.

from.description: First day, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC; default 30 days before `to`)

tools.name: get_app_repository
tools.title: Where an app's code lives
tools.description: Developer: the repository an app's builds push to. By default Mynt keeps a private one for each app (managed: true), created on its first build, so you need no repository of your own; the result includes a read-only token, valid for an hour, to clone your code with. Or it's your own repository, set with set_app_repository.

tools.name: get_build
tools.title: Track a build
tools.description: Developer: one build in full: its phase, timeline, cost against the cap, the Maxwell security summary, readiness checks, preview URL and pull request.

tools.name: get_build_activity
tools.title: What the coding agent is doing
tools.description: Developer: what the coding agent did (its messages, commands and edits), kept after its sandbox stops. Without `after`, the latest entries, newest first. To follow a build, pass the `cursor` you got back as `after`: you get only what's new, oldest first, and a new cursor.

after.description: A cursor from an earlier call: only entries after it

text_deltas.description: Also return the words of a message as the agent writes it (text_delta entries, tied to the message by `stream`)

reasoning.description: Also return the agent's reasoning, scrubbed of secrets as its messages are: `thinking` entries, and with text_deltas its words as it thinks (thinking_delta entries, tied to their `thinking` entry by `stream`)

tools.name: get_campaign_metrics
tools.title: Campaign metrics
tools.description: Developer (GTM): audience size, attributed enrollments, conversion rate, and enrollments per variant and per product.

tools.name: get_chat_session
tools.title: Read a chat session
tools.description: Signed-in user: one of your chat sessions with its events in order (replay them to get the chat back); after_seq gives only the newer ones. format 'jsonl' gives the session as JSONL instead: its own line, then one line per event.

id.description: The session's id (a UUID the caller picks when it creates the session)

tools.name: get_compliance_coverage
tools.title: Where a workspace's products are covered
tools.description: Developer: for each of the 50 US states and DC, whether the workspace's apps can serve it, by Mynt's own rules (every regulated component of a product covered there by a licence in force, under an approved sponsorship where a licence provider provides it, and the product's sales not paused). unlocked: a product one of its apps uses is covered there (with the firms whose licences cover it, those licences, the products and those firms' approved money rails there). available: some other published product is covered there. unavailable: none is.

tools.name: get_data_dictionary
tools.title: Mynt's data dictionary
tools.description: Developer: the customer data fields journeys collect, with their type, validation, sensitivity (sensitive ones need a secure capture) and the ways each may be captured.

tools.name: get_default_journey
tools.title: A product's default journey
tools.description: Developer: the minimum compliant journey for a product, built from its live developer contract: its offers and documents, each consent, the fields each hosted action needs (sensitive ones in secure inputs), the provider's hosted flows, then done. Start from it and edit (check_journey, save_journey).

tools.name: get_desk_job
tools.title: A desk job
tools.description: Innovator: status, cost, outcome and pull request of one of your firm's desk jobs.

tools.name: get_developer_contract
tools.title: A product's developer contract
tools.description: Developer: exactly what you can build against on a product's live version: its offers per customer segment (eligibility, terms, rates, fees and customer-facing limits), the actions your app may trigger and where each runs (client: the provider's hosted flow on the customer's device, with the consent purpose it needs; server: idempotent calls from your backend), the lifecycle events you can listen to, the consent purposes and documents you must show. Frozen per published version; contract_hash changes when it does.

tools.name: get_developer_dashboard
tools.title: Your dashboard
tools.description: Developer: across all your workspaces' apps (or one workspace's, with workspace_id), for the last 7, 30 or 90 days (default 30): live money moved (settled, in US dollars), hand-offs and how many converted, this month's build spend against your cap, money moved per day, and each app's figures, status and last build. Live (not sandbox) only. A figure Mynt doesn't measure is null, never 0: active enrollments per app and your earnings aren't tracked yet.

tools.name: get_esign_settings
tools.title: E-signature settings
tools.description: Admin: how e-signature is set up here: the provider, whether its API key is set (by whom and when, or by the server's environment), whether its webhook is registered and where it points, test mode, and when Mynt last received an event. Never the key or the webhook's id.

tools.name: get_exploration
tools.title: An exploration
tools.description: Innovator: an exploration's status, leaderboard, dataset assumptions and spend. Without job_id, your firm's recent explorations.

tools.name: get_grc_folder
tools.title: Your GRC folder
tools.description: Innovator: your entity's GRC folder (registers and repositories, current records), one party's (party_id) or one product's (product_id: where its risk models' governance lives), with each held licence's GRC matched against it: what's answered and the gaps (no record, an owner who doesn't fill the stakeholder the regulator makes accountable, non-compliance). history: true includes superseded records.

tools.name: get_linked_accounts
tools.title: Your linked accounts
tools.description: Your verified GitHub account and crypto wallets (Solana, Ethereum) linked to your sign-in, as the identity provider knows them; manage_url is where you link or unlink them. null with a reason when the provider can't be reached or no longer has your account.

tools.name: get_mainnet_review
tools.title: A mainnet program review
tools.description: Developer: a mainnet review's status and step, every check's result (hard rules with the signals they used and their limits, static analysis, the audit agent's findings as Mynt verified them, the red team's findings and Mynt's re-run of each proof of concept), the cost, the decision, an upgrade's timelock, and its audit log. Give review_id, or program_id for its latest review.

tools.name: get_my_entity
tools.title: My firm
tools.description: Your firm: its members, its licences with their review status, its roster and GRC, and legitimacy: Mynt's own public checks that it's a real company (GLEIF's record of its LEI, FinCEN's MSB registrant list), which a licence provider must pass to sponsor products.

tools.name: get_partner_kit
tools.title: Partner kit: your ledger source and conformance
tools.description: Licence provider (your firm) or admin (any firm): where the firm's ledger is read from (sandbox, http or file) and whether it's live, its endpoints and any change an admin proposed that waits for the firm's confirmation, whether its request-signing secret was taken, its test signing key, every conformance run with its time and expiry, and its daily files' times. Never the figures. The guide for a firm's engineers is docs/partners.md.

tools.name: get_platform_settings
tools.title: Operational settings
tools.description: Admin: the operational settings this server runs with that aren't secrets (build and audit spend caps, the build audit, the exploration cap, the hosted VM hour's price): each one's value in effect, its default, and whether the server's environment sets it. Read-only: they're changed on the server, never through a tool.

tools.name: get_product
tools.title: Get a financial product
tools.description: Return full details for one product by its id (e.g. 'ppf', 'index-fund'). Innovators can also fetch their own drafts.

tools.name: get_product_definition
tools.title: A product's v2 definition
tools.description: Innovator: the saved v2 definition of one of your products (its working copy), with its current check result. Live products also show the definition hash pinned at publish.

tools.name: get_product_distribution_metrics
tools.title: How a product performs across apps
tools.description: Innovator: views, clicks and hand-offs for one of your products across every developer app that shows it, per app and per day. Live traffic only.

tools.name: get_product_health
tools.title: Product health: the numbers
tools.description: Licence provider, or a liquidity provider committed to one of the product's pools: the decrypted financial-health report of a product you're entitled to: reserves, customer obligations, coverage, flows, pending settlements, reversal and failure rates, in integer cents and basis points. A figure Mynt can't measure is null with its reason, never 0. With each snapshot, whether its report still matches its fingerprint and whether the fingerprint matches what's on chain, and the gaps in the record. Admins go through the same entitlement.

pool_id.description: A pool of the product, when pools exist

tools.name: get_product_promotion_checks
tools.title: What a product needs to move up a stage
tools.description: Innovator: the checks for promoting one of your financial products one step, idea → staging or staging → production (or a production product's pending draft version to production), the same stages as an app's, computed by Mynt from its own records. staging: test_product passed on what would go live, unchanged since. production: what publishing needs: that test, the v2 definition still checking out, a verified licence covering it (your firm's, or a licence provider's sponsorship of each component you don't provide yourself), and published underlying products. Each check is pass or fail with Mynt's detail and a fix; can_promote when all pass.

tools.name: get_product_regime
tools.title: A product's regulatory regime
tools.description: The regulated primitives a product is made of and, for each, what it falls under (regulated product types), who supervises it, which licences may provide it, the law recorded against it, who provides it and whether their licence covers it, and the stakeholders that licence mandates. A published product shows its pinned live composition and any drift; its firm and admins can pass working: true for the unpublished working copy.

tools.name: get_product_sdk
tools.title: Integration kit for a product
tools.description: Developer: what you need to build on a product: its data shape, sample data for a sandbox, the actions and hand-offs you may use, the disclosures and branding you must show, and your access status.

tools.name: get_product_take_rate
