tools.description: Developer: replace a key's secret. The old secret stops working at once; the new one is shown once.

tools.name: rotate_partner_ledger_secret
tools.title: Replace your ledger request-signing secret
tools.description: Licence provider: issue a new request-signing secret, shown once. The old one stops being used at once, so update your endpoint straight away.

tools.name: rotate_subscription_secret
tools.title: Rotate a subscriber's signing secret
tools.description: Vendor: replace a subscriber's signing secret. Mynt signs with the new one at once and the old one stops verifying. The new one is shown once, here.

tools.name: rotate_webhook_secret
tools.title: Rotate a webhook's signing secret
tools.description: Developer: a new signing secret for a webhook, shown once. Deliveries from now on are signed with it.

tools.name: run_conformance
tools.title: Have Mynt test your endpoint
tools.description: Vendor: Mynt calls your test endpoint with signed fixture requests and checks every answer against the service type's output schema, that a badly signed request is refused, and your licences. A pass lets you list the offering. If you require a credential, pass a test one; it isn't kept.

tools.name: run_firm_checks
tools.title: Check a firm is a real company
tools.description: Admin: run Mynt's public checks that a firm is a real, legitimate company, now: GLEIF's record of its LEI (identifier 'lei': legal name, jurisdiction, entity and LEI status) and FinCEN's MSB registrant list (legal name and state). Each answer is stored with its source, URL, time, matched fields and a hash. A licence provider sponsors only once they pass (SPONSOR_LEGITIMACY_RULE; default: a matching LEI or MSB registration, and no mismatch or lapse); a mismatch or lapse drifts the products it sponsors. The NMLS ID and FinCEN registration number are listed to check by hand. Licence providers' firms are re-checked monthly on their own.

tools.name: run_partner_conformance
tools.title: Have Mynt test your ledger, identity and rails
tools.description: Licence provider (your firm) or admin: Mynt tests (a) your ledger: source http calls your test endpoint with signed requests and checks the statement's schema, Ed25519 signature with your test key, clock, null handling, coverage of every product you sponsor, and that bad, stale, malformed, wrong-environment and wrong-audience requests are refused; source file checks your latest uploaded daily file the same way. (b) An identity provider you accept answers a passed test check with residential_state. (c) Your money rails' own conformance, reported. Passing (a) lets you switch to that source with set_partner_ledger_source; a pass runs out after a while (expires_at). Results are kept with their time.

tools.name: sandbox_diff
tools.title: What the agents changed
tools.description: Developer: git status and the full diff of your app in the build's sandbox, so far.

tools.name: sandbox_files
tools.title: Browse the build's files
tools.description: Developer: list a directory or read a file in your build's sandbox (paths relative to the app, e.g. 'api/src/server.ts').

tools.name: sandbox_run
tools.title: Run a command in the build's sandbox
tools.description: Developer: run a shell command in your build's sandbox, in the app's directory (e.g. 'npm test', 'docker compose ps', 'git log --oneline -5'). Output is capped and secrets are scrubbed; every command is on the build's timeline.

tools.name: save_journey
tools.title: Save a journey to an app
tools.description: Developer: save a checked journey to one of your apps (its product must be one of the app's). Devices fetch it with GET /v1/client/journeys/{journey}. It's tied to the contract version it was checked against: when the product publishes a new contract, the journey stops being served until you check and save it again.

tools.name: seed_app_ideas
tools.title: Add Mynt's shipped app ideas
tools.description: Admin: add a set of the app ideas that ship with Mynt that aren't in the database yet: seed 'v1' (the default, workspaces/coding-build/templates/ideas.seed.json) or 'v2' (ideas.v2.seed.json: sharper ideas on the same products, with new ids). Safe to run again: an idea already there, edited or retired, is never overwritten. With replace: true, every active idea not in that set is then retired (never deleted; update_app_idea with status 'active' brings one back), and the retired ids are returned. With labels_only: true, nothing is added or retired: each idea of the set already in the database that has no chip_label gets the set's (filled), one that has a chip_label keeps it (kept), and ids not in the database are listed (missing). Mynt never does this on its own.

seed.description: Which shipped set to add (default v1)

replace.description: Retire every active idea that isn't in the set (never deletes)

labels_only.description: Only fill in the set's chip_label on its ideas already there that have none; adds, retires and changes nothing else

tools.name: seed_product_ideas
tools.title: Add Mynt's shipped financial product ideas
tools.description: Admin: add the financial product ideas that ship with Mynt (workspaces/coding-build/templates/product-ideas.seed.json) that aren't in the database yet. Safe to run again: an idea already there, edited or retired, is never overwritten. With labels_only: true, nothing is added: each shipped idea already in the database that has no chip_label gets the seed's (filled), one that has a chip_label keeps it (kept), and ids not in the database are listed (missing). Mynt never does this on its own.

labels_only.description: Only fill in the seed's chip_label on its ideas already there that have none; adds and changes nothing else

tools.name: set_app_repository
tools.title: Use your own repository for an app
tools.description: Developer: from now on, the app's builds push to one of your own connected repositories instead of the one Mynt manages for it; or, given the app's own managed repository (get_app_repository names it), back to that. Builds already made stay where they are (continue_from works within one repository: push the managed repository's branch to yours first if you want to carry on from it).

tools.name: set_app_target_segments
tools.title: Choose an app's target customers
tools.description: Developer (the app's workspace owners and admins): set which customer segments (personas) the app targets, each a segment its product declares (see get_app_customers). Replaces the app's whole choice; an empty list clears it. Audited.

tools.name: set_app_target_states
tools.title: Set the US states an app serves
tools.description: Developer (the workspace's owners and admins): the US states (ISO 3166-2, e.g. 'us-ny'; 'us-dc' for DC) the app serves. Promotion to production checks that every product it uses is covered by a licence in force in each. Replaces the list; an empty list clears it.

tools.name: set_covenant
tools.title: Set a covenant on a sponsored product
tools.description: Licence provider: set a rule on a product your firm sponsors, or change one (pass covenant_id). action: 'alert' tells your firm (covenant.breached on your firm webhooks, list_covenant_breaches, ops_status); 'pause' also pauses new sales through drift, until you release it. Sandbox figures never pause anything. Rule types: coverage_below (basis points of reserves over obligations, breached below it), reversal_rate_above and failure_rate_above (basis points), unresolved_above (cents), complaints_above (a count; Mynt doesn't track complaints yet, so it reads unknown), snapshot_missed_for and unverified_for (seconds, at least two snapshot intervals), consecutive_gaps (breached at this many missed periods in a row, at least 1). A figure Mynt can't measure is status unknown with its reason: never a pass, never a breach. Takes effect from the next evaluation; every change is audited with its old and new values. Loosening a rule with an open breach needs a reason. Mynt's admins can't call this.

covenant_id.description: To change an existing rule; omit to add a new one

threshold.description: In the rule type's own unit: basis points, cents, seconds, or a count

cooldown_seconds.description: The least time between alerts of this rule. A breach still recording during it is marked; a pause never waits. Default a day

unknown_limit_seconds.description: How long this rule may read unknown before that itself alerts your firm. Default a day

reason.description: Needed when loosening a rule with an open breach

tools.name: set_entity_facts
tools.title: Update your firm's facts
tools.description: Set your firm's legal form, incorporation or identifiers (each replaces what's there). Products resting on it are re-checked.

tools.name: set_entity_status
tools.title: Set a legal entity's status
tools.description: Admin: record a legal entity's status from its company registry (active, suspended, under_liquidation, dissolved, struck_off). Every published product resting on it is re-checked, and drifted ones pause new sales.

tools.name: set_esign_api_key
tools.title: Set the e-signature API key
tools.description: Admin: set the e-signature service's API key. Mynt checks it with the service, keeps it sealed (never shown again), then registers the service's webhook to this server (reusing one already pointing here). The server's environment, where it sets a key, still takes precedence. Audited without the key.

tools.name: set_esign_test_mode
tools.title: E-signature test mode
tools.description: Admin: turn the e-signature service's test mode on or off. On (the default): documents are free and not legally binding, for trying the flow. Off: documents are legally binding and count towards the service's billing. Documents already made keep the mode they were made in. ESIGN_TEST_MODE in the server's environment, where set, takes precedence. Audited.

tools.name: set_experience
tools.title: Define an app's experience
tools.description: Developer: set the structured experience of one of your apps: screens of components (product_card, comparison_table, calculator, disclosure_block, handoff_cta, text). check_experience then checks its structure against each product's terms; publish_app refuses failures. Pass null to clear it.

tools.name: set_mynt_ramp
tools.title: Designate the Mynt Ramp
tools.description: Admin: name the firm that operates the Mynt Ramp, the one on- and off-ramp every product's fiat in and out goes through (category `ramp` service types). Today that's the licensed ramp partner, which holds funds in transit under its own licences. Only that firm may offer or list ramp services, and Mynt calls only its offerings. Omit entity_id to see the current one.

tools.name: set_partner_ledger_source
tools.title: Switch your ledger source
tools.description: Licence provider: read your firm's ledger from http (your live endpoint) or file (your daily uploads) instead of the sandbox, or go back to sandbox. Refused until that source's latest run_partner_conformance passed its ledger part and hasn't run out; switching to http also reads your live endpoint once and checks the statement, signed with your live key (the figures are discarded), and switching to file needs a fresh live daily file. Admins can only send a firm back to sandbox, and the firm is told on its webhooks. Audited.

entity_id.description: Admin: the firm to send back to sandbox

tools.name: set_pool_firm_state
tools.title: Correct a firm's state in a pool
tools.description: Admin, or the pool's sponsor: correct the US state a firm's capital moves from in this pool, when it's wrong or its rails no longer serve it. The new state must pass the money rails' own checks: a rail of this pool's, an approved sponsorship and a licence in force there. A sponsor's correction changes nothing until the firm accepts it (respond_to_state_correction). An admin's applies at once and the firm can dispute it for POOL_CORRECTION_DISPUTE_DAYS days (14 by default), which puts the old state back. A new correction replaces any earlier pending one; only a new admin's correction replaces an applied one, so a sponsor's proposal never takes away the firm's right to dispute an admin's. Either way the firm's parked requests go back to their place once it applies. An admin at the firm itself or the product's firm can't do this. Audited, with the old and new state.

tools.name: set_pool_offering_cleared
tools.title: Record that a pool's offering was cleared
tools.description: Admin: record that this pool's offering has been cleared for real commitments, and the legal basis (who advised, and on what exemption or registration). Pooled investor capital with withdrawal rights may be a securities offering, so real (non-sandbox) commitments are refused until this is set. Setting cleared to false stops new commitments; money already in stays subject to the withdrawal queue. Whoever belongs to the pool's product firm or its sponsor can't set this. Audited.

tools.name: set_product_access
tools.title: Open a product to developers
tools.description: Innovator: set who may build on one of your products. open: any developer can publish experiences that meet your terms; approval: they build now and go live when you approve; private: only developers you invite. Terms set what experiences may do and must show.

permitted_actions.description: What experiences may do with the product

required_disclosures.description: Text every experience must show, e.g. a risk warning

banned_phrases.description: Words or claims experiences must not use

allowed_personas.description: Customer persona ids the experience may target (empty: any the licence allows)

branding.description: How the product and its issuer or distributor must be labelled

handoff_url.description: Your onboarding entry point: runtime API hand-offs (deep_link, initiate_onboarding) redirect here with ?handoff_id=…&app_id=…

tools.name: set_product_composition
tools.title: Set a product's composition
tools.description: Innovator: what your product is made of, and who stands behind it. Each component is a primitive (the line: credit, payments, account_operations, …) with an action, in a country, provided by your firm (by: self, optionally naming the licence), by an external party on your firm's roster (by: party), or by a licence provider sponsoring it under its licences (by: sponsor, its firm id; then request_sponsorship). Example: a recurring deposit = payments sale (by a partner bank on your roster) + account_operations issuance (by you). parties binds roster parties to components: the stakeholders each licence you provide under mandates must be bound. Collateral, segment and purpose are business context, not components. On a published product this edits the working copy; it goes live with the next published version.

key.description: Unique in the product; parties and business context refer to it

primitive.description: The primitive is the line: credit, securitization, payments, account_operations, custody_settlement, wealth, insurance, guarantees_trade, exchange, derivatives or information

action.description: What is done with it in this product: issuance, sale, purchase, secondary_sale, repackaging, advice, servicing, underwriting or assessment (an independent rating, valuation, index, actuarial certification, audit or accreditation)

underlying.description: What it is made of, when the line alone doesn't say: cash, securities, commodities, real_assets, receivables, risk, data or digital_assets

wrapper.description: A statutory or tax structure around it: statutory_pension, tax_advantaged or government_scheme

provider.description: Who provides it. Required on a firm's product; Mynt reference products (no firm) leave it out

licence_id.description: One of your entity's held licences; omit to use whichever covers it (pinned at publish)

party_id.description: An active external party on your entity's roster (see add_party)

entity_id.description: A licence provider's firm id (shared out of band); it covers the component once it approves your request_sponsorship

offered_in.description: Where it's offered, when its country licenses state by state: ISO 3166-2 codes in its country (e.g. ['us-ny', 'us-ca']), or the country code (['us']) for the whole country, which needs a licence covering all of it. Coverage is checked in each. Omit to check the country as a whole, as before

party_id.description: A party on your entity's roster

for.description: The component key it stands behind

tools.name: set_product_definition
tools.title: Define a product (v2)
tools.description: Innovator: save the full v2 definition of one of your products: its components (line × action) and the typed links between them, segments, algorithms, risk models, partner handoffs, terms, rates, fees, limits, servicing, lifecycle events, costs and connections. It's checked as check_product_definition does and refused with every error at once. Saving sets the product's composition and parties from it (so get_product_regime and the publish checks use it) and its catalogue record from the projection; on a live product it goes into the draft version. Then test_product and publish_product as usual.

tools.name: set_product_terms
tools.title: Set a product's term sheet
tools.description: Innovator: the economics of one of your products, as named inputs (e.g. apr_pct, processing_fee_pct, tenor_months, cost_of_funds_pct, expected_pd_pct, lgd_pct, opex_pct; or premium, sum_assured, commission_pct; or ter_pct, trail_pct) plus assumptions. The desk's models say which inputs they need. Changing it makes earlier analyses stale.

tools.name: set_public_signup
tools.title: Open or close public sign-up
tools.description: Admin: when on, anyone who signs in with a verified email joins as a consumer (an invite is written for them, so they show in list_whitelist and can be revoked). Higher roles still need invite_user. People an admin revoked stay out. Also turns the sign-in provider's allowlist off (on when closing), best effort.

tools.name: set_ramp_adapter
tools.title: Run the ramp partner through an adapter
tools.description: Mynt Ramp firm or admin: answer a ramp offering through an adapter in front of the partner's own API, instead of the partner implementing Mynt's vendor wire contract. The offering's test_base_url and live_base_url are then the partner's API (for Bridge: https://api.sandbox.bridge.xyz and https://api.bridge.xyz). Credentials go sealed into the ramp firm's key vault and are never shown again; a credential left out keeps the one set. Setting it sends the offering back to draft: run_conformance again. Adapters: bridge. adapter: null goes back to the wire contract.

config.description: The adapter's non-secret settings (see the result's config_fields)

tools.name: set_subscription_live
tools.title: Turn a vendor service live
tools.description: Innovator: let live sessions call the vendor's live endpoint (live: true), or stop that (false). Sandbox sessions always use its test endpoint. Give the live credential here if the offering needs one and you haven't yet; it replaces any earlier one.

tools.name: sign_app_agreement
tools.title: Sign an app agreement
tools.description: Either side of an accepted app agreement records its signature: the app's workspace owners or admins for the app, a member of the other firm for it. It becomes signed only once both sides have. Where e-signature is configured, program agreements are signed by e-signature instead (get_agreement_signing_link) and this refuses them. Audited, and the other firm is told when it's signed.

tools.name: simulate_handoff
tools.title: Resolve a sandbox hand-off
tools.description: Developer: finish one of your app's sandbox hand-offs as completed or failed, which sends handoff.completed or handoff.failed to your webhooks.

tools.name: simulate_program_call
tools.title: Simulate a call to a Solana program
tools.description: Developer: run an instruction against one of your deployed programs without sending it: the logs, compute used and any error. Fees come from your fee payer, which no program sees; $caller is your caller key.

method.description: An Anchor instruction's name in snake_case (e.g. 'record'); Mynt adds its discriminator

data_base64.description: Instead of method: the whole instruction data, base64 (non-Anchor programs)

pubkey.description: An address, or "$caller" for your caller key (the only signer a call may have; it signs only when listed with signer: true)

instruction.description: The instruction to send to the program

tools.name: solana_build_environment
tools.title: Pre-built Solana build environment
tools.description: Admin: the snapshot Solana build and verify sandboxes boot from (the pinned toolchain installed and checked, Anchor's image pulled by digest), keyed by the toolchain pins. 'status' shows it; 'prepare' builds it now instead of on the first Solana build; 'rebuild' replaces it. Each sandbox booted from it re-hashes it against Mynt's record before use, and installs from the pinned, checksum-verified downloads on any mismatch.

tools.name: start_build
tools.title: Start a coding-agent build
tools.description: Developer: have Mynt's coding agent build or ship one of your experiences in a sandbox: it writes the code, passes a Maxwell security audit (critical/high findings block it) and a production-readiness checklist, deploys a preview and, with a connected repository, opens a pull request. Spend is capped per build and per month. Track it with get_build.

goal.description: What to build or change, in plain words

app_id.description: The experience to build (its products, terms and screens are given to the agent)

repository.description: A connected repository (owner/name) to push to. Default: the app's own repository, which Mynt creates and manages for it unless you chose yours with set_app_repository

cap_usd.description: Spend cap for this build, up to the platform maximum

solana.description: Give the agents the Solana toolchain (Agave, Anchor, Rust) to build an Anchor program beside the app; on by default when the app has programs reserved

mode.description: once (default): the agent builds and ships in one go. session: it does your first request, then stays open for your next ones (steer_build), keeping its context, until you call finish_build or it has been idle 15 minutes; then it ships and Mynt verifies it as usual. Idle time counts against the cap

continue_from.description: An earlier build of yours whose pushed branch this one starts from (same app and repository)

kind.description: An app kind to start from (list_app_kinds): the agent scaffolds the starter app with that kind's screens

tools.name: start_exploration
tools.title: Explore improvements to an algorithm
tools.description: Innovator: have several explorer agents try to improve one of a product's decision algorithms (from its core_algorithms) on synthetic applicants. Mynt scores every variant, and the version pinned now, on a holdout set the explorers never see, and ranks them. Nothing changes until you adopt one.

algorithm_id.description: The _id of one of the product's core_algorithms

max_loss_rate_pct.description: Realised loss ceiling, % of the approved amount; default: the term sheet's expected loss

apr_cap_pct.description: Default: the term sheet's apr_cap_pct or the product's lending rate cap

tools.name: steer_build
tools.title: Steer a running build
tools.description: Developer: send the coding agent an instruction mid-build (e.g. 'use the existing design system'). It interrupts the agent's current turn and becomes the next one. In a session it's your next request; once the session is finishing it's refused, and one sent at the very moment it starts finishing is held back: the build's timeline then says it wasn't delivered (steered: true means Mynt queued it, not that the agent read it).

tools.name: stop_build
tools.title: Stop a build
tools.description: Developer: stop a build now; its sandbox is stopped and billing ends.

tools.name: stop_desk_job
tools.title: Stop a desk job
tools.description: Innovator: stop a running desk job and its sandboxes.

tools.name: stop_exploration
tools.title: Stop an exploration
tools.description: Innovator: stop a running exploration and all its sandboxes.

tools.name: stop_review_case
tools.title: Stop a governance review
tools.description: Admin: stop a running review and its sandbox.

tools.name: submit_agreement_audit_evidence
tools.title: Submit evidence for an oversight audit
tools.description: Developer (the app's workspace owners and admins): submit evidence for an open oversight audit of your app: each item a name, an https link to it and its SHA-256 (Mynt stores links and hashes, not files), with an optional note. The audit becomes submitted, waiting for the licence provider's review. Audited; the licence provider is told.

tools.name: submit_partner_signature
tools.title: Co-sign a product-health snapshot
tools.description: Licence provider: co-sign a snapshot waiting for a signature (status pending_signature in list_product_health, before its window closes), while your firm still sponsors the product. Sign, with Ed25519, the UTF-8 text 'mynt.product_health.cosign.v1', one zero byte, then the 32 bytes of its fingerprint. A live product's snapshot counts as verified only when co-signed; one with no signature by the deadline is published as mynt_only, and says so. Schema: mynt.product_health.v1.

pool_id.description: A pool of the product, when pools exist

signature.description: The Ed25519 signature, hex or base58

tools.name: subscribe_vendor_service
tools.title: Subscribe to a vendor's service
tools.description: Innovator: subscribe your firm to a listed offering (in the sandbox first). When the vendor has standard terms on file (list_vendor_offerings' standard_terms), subscribing is click-through: pass accept_terms_version (the current version: you accept those terms) and app_ids, the apps it's for (your workspace's owners and admins only), optionally with products (ids of those apps' products it's used for); Mynt records one vendor agreement per app with the vendor's firm, signed by both sides (the vendor through its listing, you through this call), with the terms' version and SHA-256. Already subscribed: naming more apps adds their agreements. Checks the licences the service needs your firm to hold, keeps the test (and live) credentials the vendor gave you, if it needs them, in your firm's key vault, never shown again, and adds the vendor to your roster as a party. Then bind a partner handoff to it: handoff_to_party to that party with attributes.vendor_subscription_id. The vendor bills you directly; Mynt never bills or holds money for it.

accept_terms_version.description: The version of the vendor's standard terms you accept; must be the current one

app_ids.description: The apps the service is for (needed when the vendor has standard terms)

products.description: Ids of those apps' products the service is used for

test_credential.description: The test API credential the vendor issued your firm, if the offering requires one; sent only to its test endpoint

live_credential.description: The live credential; sent only to its live endpoint (can also be given to set_subscription_live)

tools.name: suspend_product_experiences
tools.title: Kill switch for a product
tools.description: Innovator: take one of your products out of every developer experience at once: makes it private, revokes all access grants, and pauses live campaigns that include it.

tools.name: suspend_rail
tools.title: Suspend a money rail
tools.description: Admin: Stops new movements on it at once; approve_rail puts it back. Movements already in flight aren't cancelled; they're listed in the result (in_flight), and carry on to their end in the ledger. Audited.

tools.name: suspend_tenant
tools.title: suspend tenant
tools.description: Admin: the kill switch. Cuts a developer's VM off at once (its tunnel, routes and egress are dropped from the gateway) and powers it off. Resume with resume_tenant.

tools.name: suspend_vendor_offering
tools.title: Suspend a vendor's offering
tools.description: Admin: stop an offering being listed or called (suspended: true), or lift that (false: it goes back to draft and must pass conformance again). Products bound to it drift, pausing new sales, until it's lifted.

tools.name: terminate_app_agreement
tools.title: End an app agreement
tools.description: Either side ends an app agreement that's proposed (withdrawing it), accepted or signed, with the reason. Audited, and the other firm is told. A vendor's standard terms accepted with a subscription (vendor_subscription_id): ending the last such agreement ends the subscription too, refused while live products hand off through it.

tools.name: test_product
tools.title: Test a financial product
tools.description: Innovator: run disclosure, consistency and misleading-claim checks on one of your products (admins: also Mynt's reference products). A passing report is required to publish.

tools.name: unarchive_product
tools.title: Unarchive a financial product
tools.description: Innovator: bring back one of your archived products, to the stage it was archived in (staging reopens it to sandbox builds). Audited as product_unarchived.

tools.name: unarchive_workspace
tools.title: Unarchive a workspace
tools.description: Developer: owners only. Undoes archive_workspace while its 7 days haven't passed: nobody has been removed yet.

tools.name: undeploy_app
tools.title: Stop hosting an app
tools.description: Developer: stop hosting one of your apps; its public addresses go away and, under direct hosting, its VM is deleted.

tools.name: unpublish_product
tools.title: Unpublish a financial product
tools.description: Innovator: remove one of your products from the catalog (admins: also Mynt's reference products). Existing enrollments are kept; no new ones can be made.

tools.name: unsubscribe_vendor_service
tools.title: End a vendor service
tools.description: Innovator: end your firm's subscription. Refused while a live product version hands off through it (publish a version without it first). Its credentials are deleted from your key vault, the vendor leaves your roster if it joined for this subscription, and the vendor agreements accepted with it (its standard terms) end too, the vendor told.

reason.description: Why, for the agreements it ends (default: 'Subscription ended')

tools.name: update_app
tools.title: Update an app experience
tools.description: Developer: change one of your app experiences. Only fields you pass are changed.

disclosures.description: Text the experience shows users, e.g. risk warnings the products require

actions.description: What the experience does with the products (default: display)

tools.name: update_app_idea
tools.title: Change an app idea
tools.description: Admin: change some of an app idea's fields (the ones you leave out stay). The idea as it would then be is checked whole, as create_app_idea checks it, so an idea added before chip labels needs a chip_label to change anything else. status 'active' brings back a retired idea.

chip_label.description: The chip's label on the Build page: 1 to 34 characters on one line, plain words saying what the app is ("Two-key household fund"). The problem is the chip's tooltip

problem.description: The problem: who has the problem and what it is, in plain words ("Roommates chase each other for their share of rent and bills"). No product names

pitch.description: One line: what the app does about the problem

goal.description: The goal the build starts from, which the developer edits

product_lines.description: Some or all of the kind's product lines

categories.description: Optional: the product categories in those lines the idea is for (deposits, retirement, ...; within the kind's own, if it lists some). The studio picks the published products in them

product_names.description: Optional: words from the names of the products it's for ("Money Market Account"), when a category is still too wide. The studio picks the published products in the idea's lines and categories whose names contain one

sort.description: Order within the kind, lowest first (default 0)

tools.name: update_campaign
tools.title: Update a campaign
tools.description: Developer (GTM): change a draft or paused campaign. Only fields you pass change; lint again before launching.

tools.name: update_product
tools.title: Update a draft financial product
tools.description: Innovator: edit one of your draft or unpublished products. Only fields you pass are changed; you must re-test before publishing.

category.description: A category admins have defined for this product line (see list_product_categories)

region.description: A region admins have defined: 'global' or a country code such as IN (see list_regions)

tools.name: update_product_idea
tools.title: Change a financial product idea
tools.description: Admin: change some of a product idea's fields (the ones you leave out stay). The idea as it would then be is checked whole, as create_product_idea checks it, so an idea added before chip labels needs a chip_label to change anything else. status 'active' brings back a retired idea.

chip_label.description: The chip's label on the Build page: 1 to 34 characters on one line, plain words, usually a shortened product name ("Goal-locked savings pots"). The product name and label are the chip's tooltip

label.description: The label: who needs the product and what for, in plain words ("Gig workers with uneven pay can't lock cash away for months")

product_name.description: A draft name for the product, which the firm edits

summary.description: One line: what the product is, factually

product_line.description: A product line with products in the region

category.description: A category in that line with products in the region (deposits, retirement, mutual_funds, bonds)

region.description: The region Mynt launches products in

key_features.description: The product's key features, each one line, stated as terms the firm sets

risk_level.description: Optional: prefilled in the Create product sheet

liquidity.description: Optional: prefilled in the Create product sheet

typical_horizon.description: Optional: prefilled in the Create product sheet

return_type.description: Optional: prefilled in the Create product sheet

sort.description: Order within the product line, lowest first (default 0)

tools.name: update_product_version
tools.title: Edit a draft version
tools.description: Innovator: change the draft version of one of your products. Only fields you pass change; it must be tested again before publishing.

category.description: A category admins have defined for this product line (see list_product_categories)

region.description: A region admins have defined: 'global' or a country code such as IN (see list_regions)

tools.name: update_risk
tools.title: Review a risk
tools.description: Review a risk on a register you keep (see add_risk): change its status (open, mitigating, accepted, closed), mitigation, likelihood and impact, owner, or the date it's next reviewed by. Accepting or closing a risk needs a note saying why. Only what you pass changes; every change is audited with what it was and what it became, and list_risks with risk_id shows that history.

note.description: Why: needed to accept or close a risk

tools.name: update_vendor_offering
tools.title: Change or list an offering
tools.description: Vendor: change an offering (changing an endpoint or licences sends it back to draft, to pass conformance again), or list it (listed: true, once conformance passed) or take it off the list (listed: false; current subscribers keep it). standard_terms sets your standard terms: any change is a new version, which new subscribers accept; agreements already made keep the version they accepted. Only your firm's own members set its terms.

test_base_url.description: HTTPS base URL of your test endpoint; Mynt calls POST <base>/v1/<service_type>

live_base_url.description: HTTPS base URL of your live endpoint

price.description: Your fixed price per call, for innovators to see; billing is between you and them, not through Mynt

summary.description: The terms in a few sentences, as subscribers see them before accepting

pricing_summary.description: Your pricing in words (e.g. '$0.40 per check, invoiced monthly'); you bill subscribers directly, never through Mynt

tools.name: upgrade_enrollment
tools.title: Upgrade an enrollment
tools.description: Consumer: move one of your enrollments onto the product's latest version (see upgrade_available in list_my_enrollments).

tools.name: upgrade_enrollments
tools.title: Upgrade enrollments to the live version
tools.description: Innovator: move every active enrollment in one of your products from an older version onto the live version.

tools.name: upgrade_program
tools.title: Upgrade a deployed Solana program
tools.description: Developer: replace a deployed program's code with the program Mynt built from a newer verified build. Same rules as deploy_program; the program keeps its address and its upgrade authority. On mainnet it needs an approved mainnet review of this build's program whose timelock is over (Mynt starts the upgrade itself when it ends). Runs in the background: follow it with get_program.

tools.name: upload_agreement_template
tools.title: Upload a program agreement template
tools.description: Licence provider (your firm's own licence providers only): add your firm's program agreement, which apps sign with you when you accept their program agreement. Either upload the document (source 'upload': a PDF or DOCX as base64, at most 5 MB; Mynt keeps it sealed with its SHA-256) or name a template your firm keeps at this deployment's e-signature service (source 'provider_template', with its placeholders for the two signers and field_map from Mynt's variables to the template's field ids). Attach it to one of your licences (licence_id) or sponsorships (sponsorship_id), or neither for your firm's default; the most specific active one is used. Mynt appends a program schedule stating the parties, the developer's firm, the app, the products, the states and the dates. Versions never change: a new upload under the same name is the next version and the active one. Audited.

signature_placement.description: signature_page: a signature page is added at the end; text_tags: the file carries the service's text tags

notes.description: Notes on the template, e.g. where fields go

tools.name: upload_partner_ledger_file
tools.title: Upload your signed daily ledger file
tools.description: Licence provider, for a firm without an API: upload today's statement (schemas/partner-ledger/statement.v1.schema.json, request_id null), signed with your live key (environment live) or your test key (environment test). Mynt checks the schema, the signature, that as_of isn't in the future or older than the maximum age, and that it's newer than your last file; the result says which sponsored products it leaves out. It's stored sealed: admins never see the figures. A live file is your ledger once you've switched to source file, and is checked against your current live key on every read.

tools.name: vm_access
tools.title: Log in to your hosting VM
tools.description: Developer (a workspace's owners and admins): SSH logins to the workspace's hosted apps' VMs (each app has its own) as a Linux user (in the docker group, no sudo), valid for a few hours; new logins revoke the last ones, and so does anyone leaving the workspace. Paste a command in a terminal, or use it as a VS Code Remote-SSH host. Keep them private: they're credentials. Apps' Mynt keys aren't on the VMs (they're added to calls to Mynt on the way out).

legacy.description: Your own hosting from before workspaces, instead

tools.name: whoami
tools.title: Who am I
tools.description: Return the current user, the roles they were granted and what those include (innovator and developer are one builder role, each including the other; builders are consumers). Guests can only browse.
